title: The Heron and the Crab
text:
An old heron lived beside a pond full of fish. He had grown too old and slow to catch them easily, so he thought of a trick. He stood at the edge of the water looking miserable and refused to eat.

A crab asked him what was wrong. The heron said he had heard terrible news: fishermen were coming soon to drain the pond and catch everything in it. He was sad because he would lose his food and his neighbors would die.

The fish panicked and begged the heron to save them. He offered to carry them, one at a time, to a large lake nearby where they would be safe. They eagerly agreed. Each day he took a fish in his beak, flew off to a flat rock out of sight, ate it, and came back for the next. The fish fought over whose turn was next.

One day the crab asked to go. The heron, wanting a change of diet, picked him up. As they flew, the crab saw the rock covered in fish bones and understood. He gripped the heron's neck in his claws and squeezed until the heron's head came off. Then he crawled back to the pond and told the remaining fish the truth.
lesson: When a predator offers to rescue you, ask who gains from the rescue. Check where the others who accepted ended up before you go yourself.
people: A heron, the fish of a pond, a crab
